prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: composition option 2 for a high-fidelity desktop web application comp, final canvas 1600 × 1000 landscape
Input images: Image 1 is the approved visual authority for “The Preparation Room”; preserve its warm paper, ebonized frame, editorial typography, fine-rule table, marginalia, and chess-analysis grammar. Image 2 is the content and chart reference for the Forecast Ensemble; carry over the multi-path forecast horizon, ranked candidate comparison, and season-pressure logic, but redraw all of it inside Image 1’s visual world.

Primary request: Create a shippable light-mode desktop web app UI for “EPL PICK OPTIMIZER”, season “2026–27”, “MATCHWEEK 1”. This is comp-round composition option 2. Use a slim dark left navigation rail. The main workspace above the bottom band is divided vertically: weekly ranked candidates occupy about 46% of the usable content width, and a large forecast ensemble horizon occupies about 36%, with remaining width used by the nav and rules/gutters. A continuous “SEASON MOVE TREE” spans the entire content width along the bottom. Selecting Arsenal is the active preview state: the ensemble chart and move tree visibly reform around that choice. A strong but restrained “Commit Arsenal” button is present.

Scene/backdrop: a serious predictive-modeling preparation room translated into an interface—warm analysis paper #F2EFE7, charcoal #191B1F, cobalt #2C5C9F, amber #D79B35, muted red #A74B42. Subtle authentic paper tooth, fine graphite rules, sparse pencil marginalia, and a restrained ebonized dark frame/left rail. No gradients.

Composition/framing:
- Full browser-free app viewport, straight-on, exact 8:5 landscape.
- Very slim charcoal/ebonized left nav with compact wordmark at top and items “PREPARATION”, “SEASON LINE”, “COMMITTED”, “MODEL”; Preparation active with a thin cobalt marker. At bottom: “MODEL READY” and “UPDATED 08:42”.
- Compact top strip across the content: “2026–27 / MATCHWEEK 1”, “FORECAST ISSUED 08:42”, “LIGHT”; a tiny adjacent note or theme control indicates “DARK MIRRORS THIS VIEW”, clarifying equivalent dark mode without changing the light comp.
- Left main pane: header “Choose this week’s line” with compact explanatory copy. One integrated ruled comparison table, not floating cards. Columns must be readable and say “CANDIDATE”, “IMMEDIATE”, “SEASON-AWARE”, “WIN PROB.”, “EXPECTED PTS”, “OPP. COST”, “AFFECTS”.
- Three ranked rows, with Arsenal selected and outlined in cobalt:
  1. “Arsenal vs Coventry” — immediate #1, season-aware #1, 76%, 2.43, −0.08, MW12
  2. “Man City vs Bournemouth” — immediate #2, season-aware #3, 73%, 2.37, −0.19, MW7
  3. “Liverpool vs Nott’m Forest” — immediate #3, season-aware #2, 70%, 2.30, −0.31, MW9
- Beneath table, a narrow analytical annotation: “+0.18 season EV · preserves Man City for MW7”. Pair it with small labels “BEST NOW” in amber and “BEST SEASON” in cobalt. Include a prominent cobalt “Commit Arsenal” button and a quieter text control “Inspect assumptions”.
- Right main pane: large chart titled “Forecast ensemble horizon”. Show many thin, pale charcoal uncertainty traces from MW1 through MW12. Emphasize exactly two paths: “Best now” in amber and “Best season” in cobalt. Use a clean ruled plot with y-axis “SEASON EXPECTED POINTS”, x-axis MW1–MW12, end labels around 29.6 and 30.9, and vertical event markers “CITY WINDOW / MW7” and “ARSENAL REUSE / MW12”. A compact selected-state readout says “ARSENAL SELECTED · 76% WIN · 2.43 xPTS” and “SEASON DELTA +0.18”. The active Arsenal row, chart emphasis, and bottom move tree must clearly read as one linked selection state.
- Bottom full-width band: “SEASON MOVE TREE”, a continuous chess-engine-style branching plan drawn with fine connected rules and small square move nodes. Main line: “MW1 ARS” → “MW2 CHE” → “MW3 NEW” → “MW4 TOT” → ellipsis → “MW7 MCI” → “MW9 LIV” → “MW12 ARS REUSE”. Use amber for the immediate-pressure branch, cobalt for the season-aware preserved line, muted red only for displaced/rerouted alternatives. Include a tiny legend “ACTIVE LINE / DISPLACED / ALTERNATE”. Make the bottom tree feel continuous across the full width, not a row of cards.
- Add very sparse handwritten pencil notes in margins, such as “preserve City window” and a small EV equation, never obstructing data.

Style/medium: exceptionally polished, credible production UI mockup; editorial analysis sheet meets chess engine; serif display title paired with a narrow utilitarian sans/mono only for measurements and table labels; disciplined density, generous alignment, fine rules, crisp readable text, tabular numerals. Light mode is primary while dark mode is explicitly described as a mirrored equivalent.

Constraints: exact product and fixture copy above; visually serious predictive modeling, never gambling or betting; one coherent analysis surface; no generic dashboard-card collage; no oversized hero title; no decorative illustration; no photos; no logos or club crests needed; no browser chrome; no watermark. Preserve ample but not wasteful whitespace and keep every major label legible at 1600 × 1000.
Avoid: gradients, casino/sportsbook cues, odds, money, neon, glassmorphism, pill-heavy controls, generic bento cards, rounded soft-shadow widgets, giant headings, saturated green, trophy imagery, football photography, overdone sketches, clutter, unreadable microtext.
